summary: TICKET-006 closed the three items TICKET-005 recorded as still open after the wave-35 claim/complete fix — partial issuance repair, resume deduplication, and the completion alert — and all three rely on database-enforced keys that exist only in an authored, never-applied migration. supabase/migrations/20260927120000_ticketing_issuance_slot_dedup.sql (SHA-256 b1afcbb00b025ddce4147e406b36a05f03e13995ac31a3f08d1ac1e462b6ea80) adds three nullable columns — tickets.issuance_slot, ticket_analytics_events.dedupe_key, ticket_sales.issuance_alerted_at — and two partial UNIQUE indexes over them, with a planned manifest at docs/engineering/migration-validation/20260927120000_ticketing_issuance_slot_dedup.json. Until it is applied, the deployed code keeps the pre-existing behaviour it was written to replace: 'a ticket is never issued twice for one purchase' rests on an application read, a resumed delivery re-emits funnel metrics, and the completion alert fires once per Stripe retry. CP-051 forbids this lane from applying it, and the database lane reports local Postgres cannot start (disk at 6.7 GiB free), so there is no isolated evidence either.
completed: Read the three open items off the TICKET-005 STATE.md record and confirmed each against the code: issueTicketsForOrder returned as soon as any ticket existed for the order, ticket_analytics_events had no unique key of any kind, and the order-confirmed alert had no durable marker (OptimizedNotificationService.createNotification has no idempotency handling, so the idempotency_key in the notification metadata deduped nothing).

Authored the additive migration: three nullable columns with no default, two partial UNIQUE indexes, and COMMENT ON COLUMN documenting the invariant each key protects. Every partial predicate excludes all pre-existing rows, so both indexes build over an empty set — the apply cannot fail on data and needs no CONCURRENTLY. No backfill on any key, for the same reason the completion marker had none: a historical admission has no provable issuance position and a historical metric row cannot be proven to be the first emission of a key.

Wrote the application to depend on the constraint rather than on a read: a duplicate position is absorbed as a 23505, the pre-check is explicitly an optimization that tolerates an unreadable read, and the alert is claimed with a compare-and-set that requires issuance_status = 'issued' AND issuance_alerted_at IS NULL.

Certified the behaviour locally: __tests__/ticketing/issuance-repair-dedup-alert.test.ts (19 cases) and __tests__/ticketing/issuance-slot-dedup-migration-contract.test.ts (19 cases), including that the tests fail when the issuance-slot constraint, the analytics dedupe key, the alert compare-and-set, or the partial-issuance mark is inverted.

Recorded the planned manifest with a layered plan, a pre-apply lineage check, the operator duplicate probes (GROUP BY order_id, issuance_slot HAVING count(*) > 1 and the dedupe_key equivalent), and manual-apply-pending status under CP-051.

Then clear completed_at to force a further resume and confirm the alert does not repeat.
Attach staging (then production) postflight evidence to the manifest and advance its status.
